svg.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt lineage
svg.desc: Three stacked boxes showing that Bolt is derived from the Super VL checkpoint rather than trained separately. Super VL holds 120 billion total parameters with 12 billion active at BF16 precision. Native 2-bit compression produces Bolt 74B-A9B-24GB, which fits a 24 gigabyte budget and states 256K context. Further compression produces the 4 gigabyte Bolt E4B. A panel on the right notes that the capability ceiling is inherited from the parent while compression damage is added at each step, so the comparison that matters is against other models of the same memory footprint, not the same parameter count.
svg.text: One checkpoint, three memory budgets — released 15 October 2026
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
120B total · 12B active per token · BF16
MoE · hybrid Mamba-2 / attention backbone
OpenMDW-1.1 · Hugging Face, NIM, OpenRouter
native 2-bit compression
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B-24GB
74B total · 9B active · 2-bit weights
fits a 24 GB budget · 256K stated context
llama.cpp · Ollama · LM Studio · Unsloth · vLLM
further compression
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B
4 GB · RTX PCs and Jetson
expected later in October 2026
What travels down the chain
The capability ceiling is inherited. Bolt cannot
know anything Super VL did not know; compression
removes precision, it does not add training.
Damage accumulates at every step down, and it is
not reported per step. The 24 GB row and the 4 GB
row carry the same name and different ceilings.
What this changes for selection
Parameter count stops being a proxy once bits per
weight is free to vary. 74B at 2 bits, 34B at 4 bits
and 12B at 8 bits are all roughly 24 GB of weights.
So compare candidates at equal memory, not equal
parameters — and score them on per-step tool-call
reliability at your own step count.
